description: Digital Minds is a multidisciplinary team interested in AI, data science, software, research, design, and education. We turn real-world challenges into practical, human-centered solutions through hackathons and innovation programs. We welcome collaborative, curious, and reliable teammates. Useful skills include programming, data analysis, machine learning, UI/UX, research, storytelling, and presentation. Beginners who are committed to learning are welcome.
summary:
CrewSense, developed by Digital Minds, is a browser-based prototype designed to help astronauts answer three questions: What changed? What does it mean? What should I do next?

It simulates ISS, lunar and Mars missions with 22 health indicators covering vital signs, sleep, mood, body mass, bone health and radiation exposure. Users explore an interactive body schematic, review clearly identified trends, and enter measurements and symptoms. Explainable rules highlight the most urgent finding and provide illustrative guidance on monitoring, action and flight-surgeon escalation. English and Arabic interfaces make the information accessible.
NASA Human Research Program and Canadian Space Agency resources inform the indicator coverage and explanations. The measurements and scenario settings are synthetic; the prototype is not clinically validated and does not transmit medical messages. CrewSense addresses the challenge through self-assessment, understandable visualization and mission-aware guidance, aiming to make onboard health information clearer when ground support is delayed.
details:
CrewSense, by Digital Minds, turns astronaut health readings into a clear next decision when ground support is delayed. Our working browser prototype simulates an ISS expedition, a lunar base and a Mars mission, tracking 22 synthetic indicators across eight systems, including vital signs, sleep, mood, body mass, bone health and radiation exposure.

Users select a mission, inspect trends, enter eight measurements and choose symptoms. Transparent, fixed-band rules return a plain-language status and illustrative next steps, including when to involve a flight surgeon. The dashboard prioritizes the worst flag, offers a flagged-only view and links a clickable 2D body to indicator explanations. Codes, units, line patterns and status glyphs distinguish signals without relying on color alone. English and Arabic interfaces support accessibility.

Built with React, TypeScript and Vite, CrewSense uses NASA HRP hazards, risks and research plus CSA resources to inform coverage and explanations. Communication-delay context supports onboard autonomy. Traces, mission settings and decision bands are prototype assumptions, not NASA patient data. No real sensor feed, messaging or clinical validation is implemented. The intended impact is clearer onboard understanding; next steps are clinician review, usability testing and secure data integration.
